title: CobSeg: Coherence Boundary Modeling for Dialogue Topic Segmentation
research_question: Can a trainable dialogue segmenter improve adjacent-utterance topic-boundary prediction by combining local lexical transitions, semantic coherence, cut informativeness, and directional boundary evidence under gold and induced supervision?
methodology: A three-branch utterance-boundary model pools semantic features, edge-weighted token features, and static topic-structure features; forms adjacent-utterance transition features; contextualizes cut positions; applies separate end/start informativeness scorers and heads; adds train-derived keyword-density logits and a class-prior bias; then decodes a binary cut sequence with a linear-chain CRF. NSP features are disabled for supervised Table 1 and enabled for pseudo-labeling. Experiments report supervised and regime-separated non-gold comparisons on five dialogue benchmarks, a direct pseudo-source analysis, supervised label-budget and component sweeps, qualitative attribution, and a GPU cost table. Exact model formulas were visually inspected in PDF pages 2–5 because the rough conversion damages equation layout. See T12-F01–F08 and topic02.metrics for locators and scope.

key_findings.finding: CobSeg evaluates binary topic-boundary detection at adjacent utterance cuts and derives contiguous dialogue segments. Token-level lexical modeling does not make its output an exact token-span, overlapping membership, or recurring-Topic assignment.

key_findings.finding: The method combines semantic, lexical, and topic-structure branches; edge-weighted token pooling; direction-specific end/start heads; cut informativeness weighting; and a linear-chain CRF. These are internal features for utterance-boundary prediction. The optional NSP channel is off in Table 1 and on in the pseudo-label setting.

key_findings.finding: In Table 1, CobSeg has the lowest reported Pk and WindowDiff on all five supervised benchmarks and the highest boundary F1 on three. On Doc2Dial its Pk/WD/F1 are 23.8/25.1/72.4, versus RoBERTa 27.7/29.6/86.7. On SuperSeg they are 19.2/20.2/80.3, versus TextSeg 24.1/25.9/85.0. This is a disagreement between metrics, not evidence that work-text scope is preserved.
key_findings.quote: CobSeg achieves the lowest Pk and Wd on 5 of 5 datasets and the highest F1 on 3 of 5 datasets.

key_findings.finding: Table 2 supports the qualified claim of lowest reported Pk/WD among methods without test-time LLM calls on VHF, DialSeg711, Doc2Dial, and TIAGE. It does not support an all-dataset or all-metric win. On SuperSeg, CobSeg is 40.7/42.5/52.4, UUPRP is 39.5/40.0/0.4, DialSTART is 39.1/45.4/48.5, and SumSeg is 49.6/50.0/57.0. Direct LLM inference is a separate regime.
key_findings.quote: Overall, CobSeg pseudo-label achieves the strongest performance among inference-free meth- ods on most datasets. It obtains the best Pk and Wd on VHF, DialSeg711, Doc2Dial, and TIAGE, with especially large gains on VHF. It also achieves the best F1 on VHF and TIAGE, and remains compet- itive on DialSeg711 and Doc2Dial, although Dy- namicCOCO gives higher F1 on these two datasets.

key_findings.finding: Pseudo-label training uses NSP plus TextTiling initialization, samples 100 training dialogues, uses an LLM to label and summarize provisional segments, and reconstructs new dialogues with specified segment lengths. Table 7 names deepseek-v4-pro. Only the reconstruction stage avoids original dialogue text; the label-summary stage receives it. No LLM calls at segmentation inference does not mean LLM-free training or a measured privacy benefit.

key_findings.finding: The supervised test sweep is dataset-dependent and nonmonotonic. DialSeg711 reaches Pk/WD/F1 3.7/4.5/94.5 at 3% training data versus 1.0/1.4/98.4 at 100%; VHF worsens from 5.9/6.8/91.1 at 25% to 7.6/9.1/88.7 at 50%. The paper does not report sampled dialogue counts per fraction, repeated subsamples, or annotation time, so this does not establish an email labeling budget.

The paper attributes stronger downstream pseudo-label results primarily to the segmenter architecture and calls induction quality the main bottleneck. Table 3 reports no CobSeg reconstruction row despite prose saying those boundaries were evaluated. The table therefore does not establish that causal attribution or the asserted comparability of reconstructed boundaries to the listed sources.

key_findings.finding: The paper motivates use under efficiency, reproducibility, deployment-cost, and privacy constraints. It provides a GPU cost table and qualitative token attribution, but no evaluation of business email, preservation of decision-bearing conditions/evidence/scope, overlapping or discontinuous Topic assignment, or privacy outcomes. These applications remain transfer hypotheses.
key_findings.quote: broadly, CobSeg should be viewed as a compact trainable boundary model rather than a replacement for direct LLM reasoning: unlike prompt-based LLM inference, it performs segmentation with a learned model and is most useful when efficiency, reproducibility, controllability, deployment cost, or privacy constraints matter.

confidence_score_semantics: Confidence in the stated evidence assessment, including absence/contradiction assessments; not the probability that an unsupported author claim is true. Scores are analyst judgments, not calibrated statistical intervals.
raw_claims: No segmenter is trained in this analysis; the goal is to measure induction quality alone.
The label-summary stage receives all provisional segments of a dialogue and outputs one pseudo label and one pseudo summary for each segment.
The LLM processes the entire provisional dialogue structure at once, preserving segment order and keeping the number of segments unchanged.
The reconstruction stage generates a complete di- alogue from segment metadata alone.
The constrained prompts ensure that the LLM produces dialogues with exact segment boundaries.

annotation_unit.gold: Utterance-to-utterance topic cuts in existing dialogue benchmarks; reference segmentation is a contiguous partition as consumed by this study. No token-span annotation study is described.
annotation_unit.pseudo: Provisional utterance segments, then generated utterance counts specify contiguous synthetic segments.

prediction_unit.unit: One binary boundary decision y_t at each candidate cut t between u_t and u_(t+1), for T-1 cuts; CRF structured decoding.
prediction_unit.token_weights: Token attribution and edge-aware pooling are internal features, not membership labels or predicted span endpoints.

contiguity.gold: Contiguous reference segmentation in the evaluated task; original datasets may have richer annotations, but this paper does not document or evaluate their use.
contiguity.prediction: A contiguous partition of one ordered dialogue; no non-sequential Topic-cluster output.
contiguity.recurrence: No identity link merges separated segments that revisit one concrete work matter.

gold.segment_membership: One partition segment per utterance in the evaluated reference representation.
gold.semantic_Topic_memberships: Not reported; no multi-label or multiple-membership gold evaluation.

prediction.segment_membership: One contiguous partition segment per utterance.
prediction.semantic_Topic_memberships: No Topic identity/classifier output; multiple Topic memberships per span are unsupported by this interface.

label_cardinality.pseudo_labels: One pseudo_label and one pseudo_summary per provisional segment. This auxiliary single-label constraint is not evidence of semantic single-topic truth.

gold.within_one_message: Not reported/evaluated; no grouping of separated spans in one message into one semantic object.
gold.thread_or_dialogue_level: Only sequential reference cuts are evaluated; recurring semantic Topic identities across separated turns are not documented.

prediction.within_one_message: Unsupported; no within-utterance span splitting or discontinuous span object.
prediction.thread_or_dialogue_level: Unsupported as a recurring Topic object; two separated segments are not linked by the CRF.

Pk.paper_definition: Named and cited to Beeferman et al. (1999); formula and window choice not reported.
Pk.analyst_conceptual_definition: For a fixed window, the fraction of valid endpoint pairs whose same-segment versus different-segment relation disagrees between prediction and gold.
Pk.denominator: Exact denominator not reported; conventionally the number of valid windows (T-k for a T-utterance sequence under one common indexing convention). Exact k, endpoint convention, short-dialogue handling, and corpus averaging are unknown.

WindowDiff.paper_definition: Called Wd and cited to Pevzner and Hearst (2002); formula and window choice not reported.
WindowDiff.analyst_conceptual_definition: For a fixed window, the fraction of valid windows in which predicted and gold boundary counts differ.
WindowDiff.denominator: Exact denominator, window width, corpus weighting, and terminal-boundary handling not reported.

boundary_F1.paper_definition: Boundary F1 is named; matching tolerance, averaging, zero-boundary convention, and precise terminal-boundary treatment are not reported.
boundary_F1.analyst_conceptual_definition: For exact positive-boundary matching, 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN); this is a conceptual definition, not a verified description of this implementation.
boundary_F1.denominator: Exact TP/FP/FN counts and averaging population not reported; not a token-span or multi-label F1.

metrics.units: Scores are retained on the displayed 0–100 scale. The paper describes differences as points but does not explicitly specify percentage normalization in the metric definition. No relative percent gain is inferred.
metrics.aggregation_and_uncertainty: Corpus aggregation is unspecified. Only Table 1 has a ± row, with undefined statistic and repeat population. No significance test is reported.
metrics.missing_value_semantics: null represents a printed dash (not available), not zero performance or a negative result.

material_inconsistencies.description: Four WD < Pk cases are listed in T12-F10. If Pk and WD use the same window width, valid windows, example weights, and standard contiguous partitions, every Pk mismatch entails a boundary-count mismatch, so WD cannot be smaller. This is a conditional diagnostic, not proof of a particular implementation error. Window widths, aggregation, terminal-boundary conventions, and library/version are absent.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retained as printed; no code, outside-paper verification, or guessed correction.

material_inconsistencies.description: Section 3.3 says reconstructed CobSeg pseudo-boundaries are evaluated against gold test annotations under the same protocol. Table 3 contains only TeT, +Glove, +CLS, +NSP, DialSTART, and DyDTS. There is no CobSeg row or numerical reconstruction-quality result. Appendix G reconstructs entirely new dialogues, so alignment of their constructed boundaries to original gold test annotations is also unexplained. The 100-dialogue evaluation sample identities and relation to the training sample are not supplied.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retained as printed; no code, outside-paper verification, or guessed correction.

RQ1.assessment: Supports testing edge-token and direction features for a fixed utterance unit; does not choose an annotation unit.

RQ2.assessment: No email/asynchronous clustering or interleaving identities; sequential dialogue boundaries only.

RQ3.level: negative capability evidence, not performance failure
RQ3.assessment: Evaluated partition and prediction interface do not express multi-membership, within-message overlap, or discontinuous Topic evidence. Richer underlying gold annotations are not documented.

RQ4.assessment: Internal token representations are not an overlapping/discontinuous span method.

RQ5.assessment: No preservation or scope-loss experiment; risks to conditions/scope remain proposals to test.

RQ6.assessment: Retain Pk, WD, and boundary F1 separately; conditional anomalies, missing definitions, and metric tradeoffs prevent unqualified ranking.

RQ7.assessment: Split counts and training settings are useful; IAA, duplicate controls, baseline provenance, and long-input handling remain incomplete.

RQ8.assessment: Investigate local lexical/directional cues, controlled label budgets, metric audits, and source-preserving email evaluation; no architecture approval.

interpretation.statement: Use CobSeg as a candidate boundary feature design. Its output does not satisfy msgloom’s required concrete-Topic membership representation by itself. Do not equate latent corpus regions with work-matter identities.

The Pk/WD versus boundary-F1 pattern is compatible with calibration or granularity differences, but it does not by itself identify the error mechanism. The paper’s calibration explanation lacks boundary-count/error decomposition and preservation tests.

No LLM at inference is a reported operating property. Pseudo training still uses an LLM, and its summary stage sees original text. The GPU table is not a measured privacy benefit or device deployment guarantee.

Gold-supervised ablations provide a more direct component comparison than the missing-row pseudo-source attribution. Reported rankings remain provisional because this is a preprint with unresolved protocol details.

proposed_experiments.proposal: Compare sentence, clause, arbitrary-span, EDU, and hybrid annotations on synthetic or user-reviewed work messages. Preserve source offsets and allow multiple Topic memberships and separated spans for one work matter. Compare annotation agreement and lost/broadened condition/evidence/scope independently of segmentation scores.

With one fixed annotation unit, encoder, data split, and tuning budget, ablate edge-token pooling, cut informativeness, and directional heads. Evaluate boundary Pk/WD/F1 and exact/overlap span assignment metrics separately. Include messages with mid-message conditions and returns to earlier work matters.

Audit metrics with explicit window widths, valid-window denominators, corpus weights, terminal-boundary rules, and raw TP/FP/FN. Check WD >= Pk only in matched settings. Report boundary-count/segment-length errors and uncertainty across independent runs.

Hold the segmenter and generated-data budget fixed when comparing provisional NSP+TeT boundaries, LLM reconstruction, and gold labels. Separate gold validation access, boundary-source quality, synthetic semantic consistency, and downstream test accuracy. Record prompts, generated counts, and duplicate controls.

Test long messages and dialogues with explicit overlength handling. Measure lost conditions and evidence after each handling choice. If the model later advances to engineering evaluation, measure the full deployed model on Raspberry Pi 5 arm64 with a stated corpus, batch size, and precision.
